plate_findings.evidence: Histopathology from the esophageal biopsy specimens was consistent acute, severe inflammation, multinucleated giant cells with nuclear molding and nuclear chromatin with a groundglass appearance

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Panel (a) is an endoscopic image demonstrating a small erosion consistent with herpes simplex esophagitis in the esophagus, as described in the caption and confirmed by histopathology. b: Panel (b) is an endoscopic image supporting the diagnosis of herpes simplex esophagitis, showing a clinical manifestation of the disease. c: Panel (c) is a histology slide (x100) showing multinucleated giant cells, characteristic of severe herpes simplex infection. d: Panel (d) is a histology slide (x600) demonstrating ground glass intranuclear inclusions, a hallmark of herpes simplex virus infection.
panels.attribution_text: Geraci et al. Herpes simplex esophagitis in immunocompetent host: a case report.. Diagnostic and therapeutic endoscopy 2009. doi:10.1155/2009/717183. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) was performed and revealed small erosion (6 mm) in the distal esophagus (Figures 1(a) and 1(b)). The rest of the endoscopic examination was normal. Multiple esophageal biopsies were obtained and sent for histopathologic examination.

Histopathology from the esophageal biopsy specimens was consistent acute, severe inflammation, multinucleated giant cells with nuclear molding and nuclear chromatin with a groundglass appearance, findings characteristic of herpes virus infection (Papanicolaou's stain, orig. mag. ×100 and ×600), typical of HSV type 1 infection (Figures 1(c) and 1(d)). Subsequent polymerase chain reaction (PCR) confirmed the diagnosis of HSE.
